title: Add utilization-over-time API for rightsizing
description:
Add a bucketed utilization-over-time API for pool rightsizing. The API must make inefficient capacity visible, such as 11 hardware-reference workers producing only about 2 worker-equivalents of actual usage.

Metric definitions:
- busy_worker_seconds = sum of task run intervals, clipped to the requested time window or bucket
- available_worker_seconds = integral over time of workers considered available
- utilization_pct = busy_worker_seconds / available_worker_seconds * 100
- worker_equivalents = busy_worker_seconds / window_seconds, representing average concurrent busy workers

Task runtime collection:
- Capture and persist the Taskcluster run resolved timestamp in addition to run_started.
- Use terminal run intervals to calculate busy time.
- Handle intervals crossing bucket boundaries by clipping them to each bucket.

Availability and capacity decisions:
- Do not maintain configured capacity manually; it is expected to drift.
- Derive availability from Taskcluster worker contact data.
- Initially consider a worker available when its last contact is within 60 minutes and it is not quarantined.
- Make the contact threshold configurable and tune it using observed last-contact ages for known healthy workers.
- Record availability transitions rather than periodic pool snapshots.
- For an offline transition, use last_contact + threshold as effective_at.
- For an online transition, use the new last_contact as effective_at.
- Quarantine and unquarantine changes must produce equivalent availability transitions.
- Transition-based storage must correctly represent a worker that disappears and later returns, while keeping storage proportional to state changes rather than polling frequency.

API expectations:
- Accept a selected time range and bucket size.
- Return pool and bucket timestamps, busy worker-hours, available worker-hours, average busy workers or worker-equivalents, utilization percentage, and data coverage metadata.
- Define utilization against available, non-quarantined workers rather than a manually configured or raw retained-worker count.
- Return null or an explicit unavailable status when the denominator is zero.

Coverage and completeness:
- Report collection_started, coverage_pct, and complete for the requested range.
- Startup incompleteness naturally disappears once the entire requested window is after collection began.
- Collection outages or missed recent-task data can create later coverage gaps, so completeness must be calculated rather than assumed.
- Avoid presenting incomplete values as authoritative rightsizing data.

Relationship to pool-classifier-49f:
- Keep job counts and jobs per active worker as separate throughput metrics. They complement utilization but cannot substitute for duration-weighted busy time.

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema migrations support resolved task times and historical availability transitions.
- Collection updates both Postgres and SQLite storage implementations with tests.
- Unit tests cover task and availability intervals crossing bucket boundaries, online/offline/return transitions, quarantine transitions, zero capacity, incomplete coverage, and configurable contact thresholds.
- API integration tests verify filtering, bucketing, formulas, stable JSON fields, and invalid parameter handling.
- API documentation states the formulas and availability semantics.
close_reason: Completed the utilization-over-time stack: task intervals, Taskcluster-derived availability transitions, coverage tracking, bucketed aggregation, versioned API, integration tests, and documentation.

title: Support listed availability for wake-on-dispatch pools
description:
Problem

All workers under the proj-autophone provisioner are wake-on-dispatch. Unlike normal workers, they do not resume Taskcluster contact after reboot until a task is dispatched. The current recent-contact policy marks them unavailable after WORKER_CONTACT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS, causing idle Android capacity to disappear from the denominator and utilization to be overstated.

Design

Add an explicit availability_mode setting to pool configuration with signal-based values:

- recent_contact: current behavior. A worker is available only while lastDateActive is within the configured contact threshold and the worker is not quarantined.
- listed: a worker returned by a successful complete listWorkers observation is treated as eligible capacity while not quarantined, regardless of lastDateActive. A worker absent from a successful complete listing becomes unavailable at observation time.

Configure every proj-autophone pool as listed. Keep recent_contact as the default for other provisioners. Implement this through configuration rather than hard-coding the provisioner name.

Semantics and limitation

For listed mode, available means eligible listed pool capacity, not confirmed live or healthy capacity. Taskcluster provides no signal that distinguishes a dormant wake-on-dispatch Android worker from a physically dead worker that remains listed. Known-bad devices must be quarantined or supplied by a future external health source; otherwise they remain in the availability denominator and can understate utilization. Task-run intervals remain the source of busy time.

API and history

Return availability_mode in utilization API responses so consumers can interpret the denominator. Define a safe cutover for already collected proj-autophone availability history so contact-derived intervals are not silently reported as listed-mode history. This may use an explicit coverage boundary, history reset procedure, or versioned semantics, but must prevent incompatible history from appearing authoritative.

Documentation and live UI

Update the utilization documentation to define both modes and clearly state the listed-mode limitation. Live pages must identify listed-mode pools and explain that availability is based on Taskcluster listing plus quarantine state, not confirmed device liveness. At minimum, surface this on the dashboard and individual pool detail pages without implying that listed workers are verified online.

Acceptance criteria

1. Pool configuration accepts and validates recent_contact and listed; recent_contact is the default.
2. All proj-autophone pools explicitly use listed.
3. Listed workers remain available despite stale or missing lastDateActive, unless quarantined.
4. Workers missing from a successful complete listWorkers observation transition out of listed availability; failed or partial observations do not create false transitions and remain coverage gaps.
5. Existing recent_contact behavior is unchanged for other pools.
6. Utilization API responses include availability_mode.
7. Pre-cutover Android history cannot be mistaken for listed-mode history.
8. Utilization API docs explain mode semantics and the dormant-versus-dead limitation.
9. Dashboard and pool detail pages disclose listed mode and its limitation.
10. Unit, storage, API, and web-page tests cover both policies, quarantine handling, disappearance, collection failure, metadata, and disclosure text.
close_reason: Implemented recent_contact and listed availability policies, safe history cutover, API metadata, UI and documentation disclosures, isolated integration fixtures, and full regression coverage; 78 tests pass.

title: Add pool utilization cards and live API guide
description:
Goal

Surface duration-weighted utilization on individual pool detail pages with a compact first version that answers common capacity questions without requiring API use. Keep the main dashboard unchanged for now. Charts and arbitrary UI range selection are explicitly out of scope for this first version.

Related work

This is related to pool-classifier-d5m (Redesign and simplify the web UI), but it is not blocked by that broader redesign and should remain independently actionable. Preserve compatibility with the existing visual language so a later redesign can move the component without changing its semantics.

Pool detail UI

Add a Utilization section containing four cards for exact trailing windows:

- 1h: trailing 1 hour
- 24h: trailing 24 hours
- 7d: trailing 7 days
- 30d: trailing 30 days, not a calendar-month interpretation

Each card displays:

- duration-weighted utilization percentage
- busy worker-hours
- available worker-hours
- coverage percentage or collection state

Calculate every percentage as total busy worker-seconds divided by total available worker-seconds for the complete window. Do not average bucket percentages and do not cap values above 100 percent. Values above 100 percent should be presented as a possible data-quality issue rather than silently normalized.

Use neutral visual styling because high utilization is not inherently good or bad. Reuse the pool availability-mode badge and the existing listed-mode limitation disclosure near the section.

Coverage and freshness

Only display a utilization percentage when the entire selected window has complete task-run and worker-availability coverage. Otherwise show an explicit state such as Collecting data with the coverage percentage. A complete window with zero available worker time should show No available capacity. Request failures should produce a per-card error state and must not prevent the rest of the pool page or other cards from rendering.

All four windows must share an end timestamp anchored to the latest common complete task and availability coverage boundary, not browser now. With periodic collection, using browser now would create an uncovered tail and make every card incomplete between polls. Display Data through TIMESTAMP plus a human-readable age so users understand freshness. Define the smallest API or storage extension needed to expose this common coverage-through timestamp; a lightweight summary endpoint is acceptable if it avoids redundant probing or repeated database work.

Loading and performance

Load utilization asynchronously so the existing pool detail page can render without waiting for utilization queries. One failed range must not fail the others. Prefer a single summary request or otherwise avoid unnecessary duplicate scans of the same 30-day task and transition history. Do not add four utilization columns or per-pool utilization queries to the main dashboard in this iteration.

Live API guide

Add a live, linked utilization API guide reachable from the Utilization section. Use a pool-aware route or equivalent context so the page can provide a copyable curl example for the current provisioner and worker type.

The guide must document:

- start, end, and bucket_seconds parameters
- inclusive start and exclusive end semantics
- response fields and units
- duration-weighted formulas
- complete, incomplete, unavailable, and coverage behavior
- recent_contact and listed availability modes
- the listed-mode dormant-versus-physically-dead limitation
- quarantine behavior
- the 90-day range and 2,000-bucket limits
- at least one pool-specific copyable curl example

Keep docs/utilization-api.md authoritative or update it alongside the live page so repository and live documentation do not drift.

Acceptance criteria

1. Every enabled pool detail page has a Utilization section with 1h, 24h, 7d, and 30d cards.
2. Cards use exact trailing windows with one shared latest-complete coverage end and display data freshness.
3. Complete cards show utilization, busy worker-hours, available worker-hours, and 100 percent coverage.
4. Incomplete windows show collection progress and no authoritative utilization percentage.
5. Zero-capacity, request-error, and greater-than-100-percent data-quality states are explicit.
6. Card percentages use aggregate worker-seconds, never averages of percentages.
7. The section loads asynchronously and does not delay or break the existing pool detail content.
8. No utilization queries or columns are added to the main dashboard.
9. Listed-mode pools retain a visible explanation that listed capacity is not confirmed device liveness.
10. A pool-aware live API guide is linked from the section and covers parameters, formulas, limits, coverage, modes, quarantine, limitations, and a copyable example.
11. Repository utilization documentation remains consistent with the live guide.
12. Route, API/storage, calculation, rendering, loading, error-state, coverage, freshness, and disclosure tests cover the feature.

comments.author: aerickson
comments.text: Investigation note: Queue listWorkers exposes worker.lastDateActive, but this is not a host boot or online timestamp. Taskcluster defines it as the last call to queue.claimWork, queue.reclaimTask, or queue.declareWorker; it is updated only every 30 minutes and may be up to 30 minutes inaccurate. It can support a coarse freshness/return inference (and declareWorker may happen after restart), but cannot measure reboot duration or dispatch readiness without observation. Existing collection stores availability transitions, lastDateActive, quarantine state, and task-run times. Prefer a provider/worker source exposing boot, reconnect, registration, or ready timestamps; otherwise distinguish inferred return from first post-recovery task start, and keep failed/partial recoveries as censored outcomes.

comments.author: aerickson
comments.text: Follow-up: explicitly research Taskcluster for a worker lifecycle timestamp such as online_since, registered_at, boot time, or a state-transition history. Check both Queue and Worker Manager/provider APIs and their event streams, not only listWorkers. If Taskcluster has no timestamp with the needed semantics and precision, ask the Taskcluster team whether a stable worker registration/online/ready event or timestamp can be exposed. Confirm whether the signal means process registration, host connectivity, or dispatch readiness before using it as the metric endpoint.

title: Expand public pool classifier API
description:
Design and implement additional versioned read-only API endpoints beyond utilization. Prioritized roadmap:

1. GET /api/v1/pools — pool discovery/config: ID, provisioner, worker type, OS, enabled state, schedule, availability mode.
2. GET /api/v1/pools/{provisioner}/{worker_type}/summary — dashboard health snapshot: worker count, alerting count, task totals, success/error rates, freshness/coverage, and availability mode.
3. GET /api/v1/pools/{provisioner}/{worker_type}/failures — failure categories/counts with a bounded time window and optional category filter.
4. GET /api/v1/pools/{provisioner}/{worker_type}/workers — per-worker activity, consecutive failures, quarantine state, and top category; support filters and pagination.
5. GET /api/v1/patterns — classification-pattern registry: name, severity, tags, description, enabled state.

Also add GET /api/v1 as a small discovery document listing endpoints and API version. Implement pool discovery plus the per-pool summary first; they enable external dashboards and automation without exposing the larger worker-level data surface. Define stable response schemas, filtering/pagination, and documentation.

title: Add observed scheduled-to-start lag metrics
description:
Implement Phase 1 of the queue-lag roadmap without requiring Pulse or a full task universe.

Collect, persist, and expose observed scheduled-to-start lag for terminal task runs already discovered through the per-worker polling path.

Scope:
- Use the Queue run timestamps: runs[].scheduled as the candidate readiness/schedulable timestamp and runs[].started as the start timestamp. Verify the exact Taskcluster semantics of scheduled before presenting it as ready_at; retain raw scheduled in storage/API even if a derived label is used.
- Calculate scheduled-to-start duration only when both timestamps are present and ordered.
- Report bounded-window count plus p50/p95 and share started within an explicit, configurable SLO. Prefer duration distributions/percentiles to an average.
- Surface the metric with the label observed start lag (or observed scheduled-to-start lag), clearly stating it covers only jobs that started and were later observed as terminal.
- Do not report a total queued-task count, drop/expiry rate, or a pool-health verdict: this collector cannot see jobs that never ran, so the metric has survivorship bias.
- Keep task/run IDs, scheduled, started, resolved, state, reasonCreated, and reasonResolved available in the data model where practical, to support a later Pulse-backed full-task ledger.
- Add unit/API/storage tests for timestamps, boundary cases, percentiles/SLO share, and the explanatory copy.

Out of scope: Pulse subscription, capture of all task dispositions, expiry/drop detection, and reconciliation; those are later roadmap phases.

title: Make collection coverage tolerate recoverable scan failures
description:
Use the retained getWorker.recentTasks window as the evidence for task-run collection coverage; reuse durable task_results lifecycle rows from vba.1/vba.2 and add no window/coverage tables.

For each worker with a nonempty current window, compare its (task_id, run_id) references with previously stored rows for that worker before recording new observations. No stored rows establishes a baseline without inferring prior coverage. Any overlap proves continuous coverage and permits ingestion of new references. Existing stored rows with a nonempty current window but no overlap creates a coverage gap because continuity cannot be proven. An empty current window requires no state or coverage update.

Keep transient Queue status failures retryable through vba.2's unresolved rows; they alone do not create a gap. Preserve Queue 404s as expired, known-unavailable outcomes. The poll interval schedules collection but is not evidence of complete coverage.

title: Test observed-run recovery and coverage semantics

title: Restore parallel Queue status collection safely
description: Restore concurrent Queue status I/O without allowing worker threads to touch classifier storage transactions. The pipeline should (1) fetch getWorker windows in parallel, (2) persist observed references/check timestamps on the classify thread, (3) fetch one Queue status per distinct task in parallel, and (4) apply statuses, expiry, and terminal classification on the classify thread. Preserve durable retry and coverage semantics.

title: Prepare observed task-run batches on the classify thread
description: Refactor observed-run handling into a main-thread preparation phase. Compute per-worker overlap continuity, persist all newly observed getWorker references, record check timestamps before Queue status requests, merge restart-safe unresolved rows, and group references by task ID while retaining worker/group routing metadata. No worker-pool code may call storage.

comments.text: Reverted the one-hour restart grace after verification showed the restart did not create a new coverage gap. The added tolerance is probably not needed and would make coverage less sensitive to real outages.

title: Show Taskcluster pools not covered by the registry
description: Add a read-only coverage/discovery page for releng-hardware and proj-autophone. Cache Taskcluster worker-type discovery, allow an authenticated/manual refetch, compare discovered worker types with pools.yaml, and separate covered, stale, intentionally excluded, and uncovered pools. For uncovered pools, provide a copyable pools.yaml snippet and instructions rather than editing Git-backed registry configuration from the UI.
close_reason: Added cached Taskcluster registry coverage page and manual refetch

title: Default pool IDs to Taskcluster worker types
description: Make pools.yaml id optional, defaulting it to worker_type in the registry loader. Remove explicit IDs, including friendly IDs that differ from worker_type, so the public pool id consistently matches the Taskcluster worker type.
close_reason: Defaulted omitted IDs to worker_type and removed explicit registry IDs

title: Add inherited defaults to pool registry
description: Support global and per-provisioner defaults in pools.yaml, merged before individual pool values. Migrate the repeated 15-minute schedule and proj-autophone listed availability mode to defaults, retain per-pool overrides, and test precedence and validation.
close_reason: Added global and per-provisioner pool defaults

title: Rename registry coverage page to Pool Discovery
description: Rename the Taskcluster-versus-registry page and navigation label to Pool Discovery, move the registry comparison explanation into the page intro, and use a pool-discovery URL.
close_reason: Renamed page, navigation, and route to Pool Discovery

title: Match Pool Discovery header to site navigation
description: Give the Pool Discovery page the shared logo, title, and hamburger navigation used by the overview and patterns pages.
close_reason: Matched Pool Discovery header and navigation to site pages

title: Centralize web navigation in a Jinja base template
description: Add a shared Jinja base template for the logo, page title, hamburger navigation, and common styles. Migrate every HTML page so Pool Discovery and future navigation changes have one source of truth.
close_reason: Centralized site header and hamburger navigation in Jinja macro

title: Add copy buttons for uncovered pool registry snippets
description: Replace inline pools.yaml snippets on Pool Discovery with per-row clipboard buttons and concise success feedback.
close_reason: Added clipboard buttons for uncovered registry entries

title: Compact and unify Pool Discovery actions
description: Use one action-button style for Pool Discovery refetch and YAML copy controls, and make uncovered-pool guidance inline rather than split across lines.
close_reason: Unified and compacted Pool Discovery actions and table layout

title: Move Pool Discovery fetch timestamp beside refetch action
description: Keep the Pool Discovery explanation separate from cache freshness by placing Last fetched beside the Refetch Taskcluster button.
close_reason: Placed fetch timestamp beside the refetch action

title: Show globally ignored VM pools in Pool Discovery
description: Classify discovered -vms worker types as globally ignored rather than uncovered, state the convention-based reason, and suppress the registry copy action.
close_reason: Marked -vms worker types as ignored in Pool Discovery

title: Migrate from pipenv to uv
description: Replace Pipfile/Pipfile.lock-based dependency management with uv. Add pyproject.toml with uv-managed deps, generate uv.lock, update dev docs/scripts/CI that invoke pipenv, and remove Pipfile/Pipfile.lock once migration is verified.

title: Replace GraphQL quarantine detail fetch with WorkerManager REST API
description: quarantine_graphql.py queried the internal/unofficial Taskcluster web-UI GraphQL endpoint to fetch quarantineDetails (reason, clientId, updatedAt) for quarantined workers. That GraphQL service is being retired. Replaced with the official taskcluster.WorkerManager().getWorker(provisionerId, workerType, workerGroup, workerId) REST call, which returns an identical quarantineDetails array. Verified data parity against production Taskcluster (same worker, same fields) before and after the switch, plus an end-to-end smoke test of _list_quarantined_workers -> _update_quarantine_cache. Deleted worker_health/quarantine_graphql.py; added self.tc_worker_manager alongside self.tc_queue in PoolClassifier._init_tc.
close_reason: Implemented and verified against production Taskcluster; code changes complete, not yet committed

title: Decide: should Pool Discovery ignore -staging pools like -vms?
description:
Open question: should worker types ending in -staging (and possibly -alpha) get the same 'ignored' treatment as -vms in Pool Discovery (registry.py is_vm_pool()/all_pools(), discovery.py status labeling)?

Findings so far: the -vms exclusion exists because those workers are short-lived and high-volume enough to overwhelm a classification cycle (POOL_CLASSIFIER.md) -- a load-management exclusion, not a relevance judgment. -staging pools are pre-production/canary hardware and are already explicitly registered+enabled in pools.yaml today (gecko-1-b-osx-1015-staging, gecko-t-osx-1015-r8-staging, gecko-t-osx-1400-r8-staging, gecko-t-osx-1500-m4-staging), all showing status=covered in live Pool Discovery.

Leaning: against a blanket ignore rule, since it would silence coverage on canary hardware before it reaches production -- but this isn't settled, revisit before acting.

Note on -alpha: two worker types (win11-64-24h2-hw-alpha, win11-64-24h2-hw-ref-alpha) are also already registered+enabled and show status=covered; a third (gecko-t-lambda-alpha-a55) is registered but currently not returned by Taskcluster (status=configured inactive). No existing -alpha exclusion logic found. Same open question applies to -alpha as to -staging.

title: Define data retention and rollups for historical pool metrics
description: Postgres data currently grows without a retention policy: task_results retains each observed task run, worker_availability_transitions retains state changes, and historical worker/quarantine records can accumulate. Assess production growth and query requirements; define retention windows and rollups that preserve dashboard/API metrics (including utilization, coverage, and observed start lag); implement safe batched pruning/partitioning or archival plus indexes; and add size/growth monitoring and operational documentation. Ensure pruning does not break freshness, windowed aggregates, or active unresolved runs.

title: Add observed start-lag p95 to overview
description: Add a sortable Lag p95 column after Utilization on the main overview. It should show the trailing 7-day observed scheduled-to-start p95 only when at least five samples are available, otherwise an em dash. Add a header tooltip that explains the observed scope and fixed window; cell hover should show p50, p95, and observed sample count. Use a batched aggregate rather than one request per overview row where practical.

title: Color overview observed lag p95 values
description: Color the main overview's observed Lag p95 text by threshold: under 2h green, 2h to under 4h yellow, 4h to under 12h orange, and 12h or more red. Keep unavailable values muted.

title: Group overview capacity columns
description: Move Hosts before Utilization and Lag p95 in the main overview table so capacity context precedes the utilization/lag pair.

title: Ignore local build and Beads coordination files
description: Add targeted ignore rules for egg-info metadata, local Beads SQLite coordination files, and macOS .DS_Store files; keep project scripts trackable.

title: Exclude unresolved observed runs from start-lag backfill
description: Restrict start-lag backfill discovery, backlog counts, and selection to rows with run_started recorded, so live observed placeholders do not cause perpetual backfill work.

title: Add local Postgres test runner
description: Add an executable script under scripts that initializes the local Postgres container, configures PC_TEST_DATABASE_URL, and runs the Postgres-backed storage and web tests.

title: Add GitHub Actions test and Docker build CI
description: Run the full pytest suite with PostgreSQL 16 on pull requests and pushes to main, and build the production Docker image in a separate CI job.

title: Fix Python 3.11 Pipenv lock for CI
description: Add the conditional Psycopg dependency typing-extensions explicitly so a fresh Python 3.11 Pipenv environment can import Psycopg and run the Postgres CI tests.

title: Upgrade runtime and CI to Python 3.14
description: Raise the supported runtime to Python 3.14 across the production Dockerfile, local migration container, GitHub Actions, package metadata, and migration documentation. Regenerate/validate the Pipenv lock under a clean Python 3.14 environment, then run the full Postgres suite and Docker build.

title: Add prek and Ruff checks
description: Add pinned prek and Ruff developer tooling, configure Git hooks, and run the checks in CI.

title: Correct misleading All Workers availability summary
description: The pool page's All Workers summary labels stored worker rows as available. It computes total_w from the persisted workers table and active_w solely as total_w minus currently quarantined worker IDs that overlap that table. This is not a live Taskcluster listing or liveness signal; quarantined worker IDs absent from the stored table are omitted from the quarantined count. Replace the statement with accurate separate counts/scopes and add regression coverage.
close_reason: Implemented tracked-worker summary and quarantine count

title: Simplify quarantine section heading
description: Remove the emoji and count from pool detail quarantine section headings; show the count as supporting text instead.

title: Make migration 007 safe and restore the production rollout
description: Incident docs/INCIDENT_20260730.md showed that migration 007 ran an unbounded historical UPDATE over approximately 1.07 million task_results rows while schema locks were held in the web startup transaction. Make the migration deploy-safe: remove historical DML from startup migration 007; limit the startup transaction to adding observed_at and last_checked_at; configure conservative lock_timeout and statement_timeout values; retain serialized migration execution; and add regression coverage using a populated table. Do not create idx_task_results_unresolved in the transaction-wrapped startup migration. Add a nontransactional database-maintenance command that uses autocommit and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS, plus the Cloud Run Job configuration or documented update procedure needed to run that command with the production DATABASE_URL, service account, and VPC connectivity. For the corrected release, document and execute an explicit manual gcloud run jobs execute --wait step after the columns and migration record exist; fail visibly on job error; and verify that the index exists and is valid before considering the index work complete. The later pool-classifier-pyo task may generalize this into a gated pre-deployment workflow, but fuo owns creating the index during the recovery rollout. Document the migration policy that startup/schema migrations must contain only bounded, fast schema work and that historical data changes and heavyweight index work require separate execution paths and explicit review. Acceptance includes releasing the correction, verifying the expected columns and migration record in production, confirming the new Cloud Run revision becomes healthy, running and verifying the concurrent index job, and checking recent warning and lock logs.
close_reason: Released v1.1.6; migration 007 applied via maintenance job, concurrent index verified, and production revision healthy

title: Add a resumable batched backfill for task observation timestamps
description: Create an independently triggered operation in the shared pool-classifier-db-maintenance Cloud Run Job to backfill task_results.observed_at and task_results.last_checked_at after the deploy-safe schema migration. Process bounded, committed batches ordered by the task_results primary-key tuple, but retain no state file or durable cursor: each batch reselects only rows whose values are still NULL, so interruption and restart are safe and cannot skip unfinished rows. Include configurable batch size, pacing, retries, optional maximum batches, structured progress/error reporting, dry-run and count-only visibility, and a final verification that reports remaining NULL rows. Document how to select, trigger, and monitor the operation independently of web-service rollout.
close_reason: Implemented and documented NULL-driven, resumable migration-007 timestamp backfill through the shared maintenance job

title: Identify PostgreSQL connections by revision, instance, and workload
description: Set PostgreSQL application_name on every pooled and direct application connection so pg_stat_activity can map backend PIDs to Cloud Run revision, instance, and workload. Include K_REVISION and HOSTNAME when present and distinguish roles such as web, classifier, migration, and advisory-lock connections. Cover the shared psycopg pool plus direct connections used by global dashboard queries, migrations, and classification locks. Add tests for deterministic fallback values outside Cloud Run and document how operators use the names during lock and slow-query diagnosis.

title: Separate production schema migrations from web-service startup
description: PostgresStorage.init_schema currently invokes apply_migrations while initializing application storage, coupling Cloud Run readiness and normal traffic to database migration duration. Move production schema migration execution to an explicit pre-deploy Cloud Run job or equivalently gated deployment step. A migration failure must stop the rollout before traffic reaches the new revision, and application instances must not perform production migrations during startup. Preserve concurrency protection and provide clear failure output. Document the migration and release policy, including schema-only bounded migrations, separate operational paths for historical data changes and heavyweight index work, required review checks, rollback expectations, and production verification steps. Add tests or CI safeguards that exercise the production migration path.
notes: Release discovery from fuo: a 0%-traffic Cloud Run revision does not start an application instance, so it cannot apply startup migrations. Implement a dedicated pool-classifier-migrate Cloud Run Job, separate from index/backfill maintenance jobs. Initial scope remains a documented, explicit manual gate: build immutable image; update the migration job to that image; execute it with --wait; verify migration state; deploy a no-traffic candidate; then promote traffic. Remove both web-service migration paths: docker-entrypoint.sh and PostgresStorage.init_schema(). Add regression coverage proving web startup never invokes apply_migrations. Preserve serialized migration execution and make migrations additive/backward-compatible so a failed candidate can roll back safely. Cloud Build automation is a future enhancement, not required by this task.
close_reason: Released v1.1.7; dedicated migration job ran successfully before no-traffic candidate promotion

title: Make the database-maintenance job dispatch reviewed operations
description: Refactor the existing pool-classifier-db-maintenance Cloud Run Job from a hard-wired concurrent-index command into a generic, explicitly triggered dispatcher. Terraform must define the durable runner, credentials, secret access, and VPC path once; later reviewed maintenance operations must be selected per execution from the release image, without a Terraform edit or configuration drift. Preserve the current migration-007 unresolved-index operation. Emit structured operation identity/progress so Cloud Logging provides operational traceability. Document invocation and safety constraints, including that ordinary bounded schema migrations continue to use the existing pool-classifier-migrate job and likewise do not require Terraform changes. Infrastructure changes remain reserved for genuine platform requirements such as permissions, networking, or execution resources. This shared plumbing is required before pool-classifier-zyw can run the migration-007 timestamp backfill through the existing maintenance job.
close_reason: Implemented durable allowlisted maintenance dispatcher and documented per-execution operation selection

title: Monitor and complete the production migration-007 timestamp backfill
description: Track the long-running production operation that backfills task_results.observed_at and task_results.last_checked_at through pool-classifier-db-maintenance. Current execution: pool-classifier-db-maintenance-dcr7m, using the v1.1.10 image, 1,000-row committed batches, pacing, and retry. Approximately 1,056,242 rows remained before the current long execution. Monitor Cloud Run execution status, database health (memory, CPU, disk latency, errors), and structured progress logs. If an execution stops or times out, safely rerun the same NULL-driven operation. Complete only after --count-only reports zero remaining NULL rows and recent service/job warning logs are reviewed.

title: Make production web UI responsive at production scale
description: Address the production latency caused by unbounded historical aggregation, request fan-out, per-worker query patterns, request-time Taskcluster calls, and chart loading. Keep metric storage flexible while the app evolves: prefer bounded queries and short-lived caches before persisted rollups.

title: Limit overview utilization to displayed windows
description: Allow utilization summaries to request an explicit window set. Make the overview request only 1h and 24h data; preserve 7d/30d support for detail pages that display those cards. Add regression coverage for window selection and bounded record retrieval.
close_reason: Completed: summary API supports bounded windows and overview requests only 1h/24h

title: Cache dynamic overview aggregates with a short TTL
description: Add short-lived, process-local caching for overview utilization and global aggregate results. Prefer TTL/invalidation over persisted rollup tables while metric definitions are evolving. Ensure keys include the requested window set and pool identity.

title: Prevent overview request fan-out from saturating the service
description: Bound the overview browser utilization requests to a small concurrency level or replace them with a cached batch endpoint. Preserve progressive rendering and avoid a single page load consuming all Gunicorn threads and database connections.

title: Replace detail-page unbounded and per-worker database queries
description: Remove the detail page N+1 worker-category queries, bound success-rate aggregation to its displayed seven-day range, and consolidate per-category top-offender queries. Verify plans and production-sized behavior with focused tests.
close_reason: Completed: batched worker categories and offenders; bounded detail success-rate query

title: Remove Taskcluster calls from detail-page rendering
description: Render quarantine information from the stored cache only. Move any refresh work to classification or another background path so detail-page latency does not depend on Taskcluster.
close_reason: Completed: detail pages use current availability snapshots and cached quarantine metadata without Taskcluster calls

title: Defer long-range detail charts until after initial render
description: Keep detail pages interactive before loading expensive utilization and observed-start-lag visualizations. Load long-range data progressively or on explicit interaction, with graceful loading and error states.

title: Replace overview utilization fan-out with a cached batch endpoint
description: Add a server-side overview utilization endpoint that returns the 1h and 24h utilization summaries for every displayed enabled pool in one request. Back the assembled response with the existing short-lived, process-local aggregate cache; preserve pool and requested-window cache scoping, and avoid persisted rollups while metric definitions evolve. Update the overview client to make one batch request, retain progressive/error-safe rendering, and add regression coverage showing that a page load no longer creates one utilization request per pool.

title: Bound cold batch utilization aggregation to four database queries
description: Make the overview utilization batch endpoint aggregate cold per-pool summaries with bounded server-side parallelism. Cap concurrent PostgreSQL work at four, matching the previously deployed browser request ceiling and staying below the per-instance pool maximum of five. Preserve the process-local batch TTL cache and per-pool summary cache, avoid unbounded fan-out, and add regression coverage for the concurrency bound.

title: Tune Cloud Run and database concurrency for overview aggregation
description: Make production concurrency settings explicit: configure 12 Gunicorn threads, an eight-connection PostgreSQL pool, and six bounded cold overview-utilization aggregation workers. Release the cached batch overview endpoint with these settings, then compare request latency and database connection usage before any further increase.

title: Add repeatable local web-performance benchmark
description: Provide a local benchmark utility that captures cold-ish and warm request timings for the overview, batch utilization response, detail HTML, and detail follow-up APIs. Save machine-readable JSON baselines before query-shape changes and compare median/p95 timings before deployment.
